planned_spool.also_planned_if_any_filled_comment: A spool missing Planned Start is normally Unplanned. But if it has already been Packed and/or Dispatched, it clearly WAS worked and completed - it's just missing from the planning sheet (e.g. added outside the normal planning cycle). Counting it as Unplanned would misrepresent real backlog, so any spool with a value in one of these fields is treated as Planned too, even without a Planned Start date.

line_history_override.comment: When a spool's Composite Key is found in the uploaded Line History Sheet with at least one non-blank Joint No. row, its joint-level classification (see merge.py -> summarize_line_history()) is one of: 'Fit-Up' (no joint has an effective Weld FitUp Date and no joint has a Welding FRun Date - nothing started), 'Partial Fit-Up/Welding' (a genuine mix - some joints done, some not), 'Welding' (every joint has an effective Weld FitUp Date, but at least one is still waiting on its Welding FRun Date - shown as status message 'Waiting for Welding', unchanged), or 'PDQC' (every joint has both). 'Effective' Weld FitUp Date means the joint's own Weld FitUp Date, or - only when that's blank - its Welding FRun Date used in its place (you cannot weld an un-fit-up joint, so a logged weld run date is itself evidence the fit-up happened even if that field wasn't separately filled in). As of 2026-08-10 this classification is AUTHORITATIVE for the Fit-Up/Partial Fit-Up-Welding/Welding band - it can both promote AND demote a spool's Current Stage relative to the DPR/Weekly's own, coarser First Fit-Up/First Welding fields (which only need ONE joint recorded to fire) - UNLESS the DPR/Weekly data already shows the spool has reached PDQC or any stage after it via its own date fields, in which case that independent evidence wins outright regardless of Line History. The last entry in override_stage_order (PDQC) is where the override stops either way - PDQC/RFP/PDI/Packing/Dispatch are always decided by the normal date-field-based logic below. If the Composite Key isn't found in the sheet, or has no non-blank Joint No. rows, the existing date-field-based logic is used unchanged for that spool. See business_rules.py -> is_stage_reached_with_line_history().

packing_dispatch_merge.comment: Backfills PDI / Packing / Dispatch on the DPR master dataset from the separate Packing & Dispatch workbooks (data/upload/packing/), matched by Composite Key (Project Code + Drawing No + Spool No - the packing workbook's own spool_no is stripped of its drawing-revision prefix, e.g. 'spool_ext_no', before matching). A DPR field is overwritten with the packing workbook's value ONLY when that value is present (non-blank) - a blank in the packing workbook never clears a value the DPR master already has. See merge.py -> apply_packing_dates().

completed.also_completed_if_any_filled_comment: A spool is normally Completed once Packing has a date. But some spools are already Packed/Dispatched in reality and just missing a Packing entry on the DPR (e.g. entered straight to Dispatch) - especially spools that were never in the planning sheet to begin with. Counting only Packing here would understate the real Completed total, so any spool with a value in one of these fields is treated as Completed too, even without a Packing date.
